items.title: Dow Jones Futures: Nasdaq Hits New High; Sandisk, Micron Trigger Buy Signals
items.summary: The Nasdaq hit a new high with memory giants Sandisk and Micron flashing buy signals. But financials are struggling.

items.title: Stock Market Today: Dow Skids But Apple Eyes A Buy Point; Filing Says Trump Makes These Trades
items.summary: The Dow Jones index fell on the stock market today after President Trump threatened Iran. Other major indexes rose. Apple was among stocks trading near buy points.

items.title: Has Arista Networks Stock Quietly Become A Different Bet?
items.summary: Investors pay 64 times earnings for Arista Networks (ANET). The S&P 500 trades at 22.5 times. They pay more because they expect fast growth to last, and for that to make sense, two things must both hold. Arista must get enough parts to ship its orders, and buying those parts must not squeeze its margins. The way management talks about its supply chain has changed. So what did it use to say.

items.title: Cisco Sinks 6% While the Tech Sector Rises; Arista and Ciena Hold Flat
items.summary: Cisco is sliding 6% while its closest networking rivals barely flinch and the broader tech sector actually gains ground, and no company announcement explains why the stock is moving alone.

items.title: Can Dell's Margins Catch Up With Its Stock?
items.summary: Dell Technologies (DELL) stock has returned 341% over the past twelve months, the best record among the six companies in its peer group. Its revenue growth also ranks first. Its operating margin ranks only fourth, and that gap is what a buyer today has to judge. Behind the growth is demand for its servers that has outrun its own supply.

items.title: Will This Major Industry Showcase Boost Quantum Computing Stocks?
items.summary: Quantum computing stocks are struggling with a major industry conference on tap as investors eye roadmap to commercialization.

items.title: How Far Could Zoom Communications Stock Fall In A Real Market Shock?
items.summary: Zoom Communications (ZM) stock sits about 21% below its 52-week high after falling 17.4% over the past month, a month in which its quarterly report beat its own guidance. Over the past year it returned 2.9% while the S&P 500 returned 17.3%. The question for a holder is what a real market shock would add.
